en_summary: Advanced Micro Devices $AMD just registered up to 336.9 million shares for resale, and the headline number looks a lot scarier than it is. Per the S-3 filed today, 320 million of those shares come from the OpenAI and Meta warrants, 160 million each.
text:
Advanced Micro Devices $AMD just registered up to 336.9 million shares for resale, and the headline number looks a lot scarier than it is.

Per the S-3 filed today, 320 million of those shares come from the OpenAI and Meta warrants, 160 million each at a $0.01 exercise price. They only vest in tranches as each company buys AMD Instinct GPUs, starting at the first gigawatt and fully vesting at 6 gigawatts, and they also need AMD stock price targets that climb to $600 for the final tranche. AMD is registering them under piggyback registration rights.

The rest, about 16.9 million shares, belongs to the sellers of Taalas and World Labs, the two AI startups AMD closed this month, and part of the Taalas piece is contingent.

Why it matters: this is paperwork that lets holders sell once shares exist, not a new stock sale, and AMD gets no proceeds. The real near term overhang is roughly 17 million acquisition shares. The 320 million only show up if OpenAI and Meta actually take up to 12 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs combined, and at that point most AMD holders would gladly take that dilution.

text:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise $HPE just grew revenue 50% and guided next year far above the Street, and the stock still slipped after hours.

FY Q4 revenue was $14.55B, up 50%, vs $14.45B market consensus. Adjusted EPS was $1.43 vs $1.29 market consensus and above HPE's own $1.20 to $1.30 guide. Server revenue hit $8.8B, up 94.7%, and Cloud & AI operating margin doubled to 18.4% from 9.3%. HPE says Q4 orders grew almost 90%, faster than revenue.

The guide is the real story. Q1 revenue of $14.0B to $14.6B vs $13.09B market consensus, adjusted EPS $1.30 to $1.40 vs $1.10. FY27 revenue raised to $59.4B to $63.1B vs $55.12B market consensus, adjusted EPS $5.05 to $5.35 vs $4.74, and free cash flow of at least $5.5B. Plus another $5B of buyback authorization, about $7.3B total, and a $0.17 dividend.

"We have a perfect portfolio to capture that inflection point across networking, cloud and AI," Antonio Neri told MarketWatch, adding that memory, flash and networking supply should stay tight into the back half of 2028.

Why it matters: servers nearly doubling with orders running ahead of sales says AI server demand is still accelerating, and tight memory supply into 2028 is one more tailwind for the memory names. The after hours dip of roughly 5-6% comes after the stock ran about 17% today with the rest of AI.

COMMENTARY  

What a Corporate Scandal Says About Our Bull Market  
By Doug Kass  
Nov 20, 2026 12:06 pm EST

Scandals like Nvidia’s inevitably emerge as markets peak.   

It always happens at the end of an economic expansion, as a bull market begins to wind  down: The risks, the frauds, and the corrupt suddenly appear in broad daylight.  

Sometimes they come in the form of overexuberant corporate executives who have been quietly skating on the thin ice of business ethics, like former Nvidia     CEO Jensen Huang. 

Or they emerge from within our country’s leadership, when figures like  former plumber, now Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin and former reality TV  star, now Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, are exposed as incompetent lackeys. 

But the truth  always surfaces when the tides go out.  Major scandals featuring questionable figures—Enron, WorldCom, Tyco, Countrywide  Credit, Joe Granville, the savings and loan crisis—all appeared late in their respective  economic and market cycles.  

Seen in this light, the recent revelation of the Nvidia CEO’s affairs with an executive at the  firm and an alleged Chinese spy, and his company’s sales to the latter’s Singapore-based  shell company, which potentially routed banned Nvidia chips to China,

text:
CROWDSTRIKE TO ACQUIRE ZSCALER FOR $43.9 BILLION

$CRWD has agreed to acquire $ZS in an all-stock deal, at $43.9B, surpassing Google's $32B acquisition of Wiz as the largest cybersecurity acquisition in history.

Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share held, valuing Zscaler at approximately $260 per share, a 34% premium to Friday's closing price.

The combined company will have more than $10B in annual recurring revenue. CrowdStrike says the deal adds over $185B to its addressable market and creates opportunities to cross-sell its cybersecurity products to roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers.

text:
Korean media report that Samsung plans to add a production line capable of processing 20,000 wafers per month at its X2 NAND flash fab in Xi’an, China, bringing the fab to its full production capacity.

X2 currently produces 100,000 V6 NAND wafers and 10,000 V9 NAND wafers per month. The fab can handle up to 130,000 wafers per month.

Samsung plans to dedicate the new line entirely to V9 and convert 20–30% of its existing V6 capacity to V9 production. The expansion and conversion would raise X2’s V9 capacity to 50,000–60,000 wafers per month.

Samsung plans to build an electroplating line in unused cleanroom space at X2, with equipment move-in expected around February 2027. The company plans to send engineers from its South Korean operations to Xi’an with the aim of completing the expansion by November 2027.

After a brutal week in the market, it is easy to believe that things can only get worse. But history offers a different perspective.

Since 1950, the S&P 500 has experienced 81 comparable sessions with losses of at least 3.5% for which forward-return data is available. Historically, the median return following those sessions was +1.80% after one month, +6.44% after three months, and +21.73% after one year. The index finished higher in 64.2% of cases after one month, 74.1% after three months, and 82.7% after one year.

That doesn’t mean the bottom is in. Some of the biggest rebounds in history happened during bear markets, only to be followed by another leg lower. A sharp bounce can mark the beginning of a recovery, or simply provide temporary relief before more pain. The difference is what happens afterward.

Right now, I am watching market breadth, volatility, yields, and whether earnings expectations remain intact. Another retest of the lows would not surprise me. Markets rarely move in a straight line from panic to recovery.

But one terrible week, one brutal selloff, or even a period of extreme fear does not determine the next 12 months. Historically, the longer the investment horizon, the more recovery has favored patient investors.

Don’t confuse uncertainty with the absence of opportunity. Protect your capital, keep some cash, avoid emotional decisions, and let the market show you when conditions are improving.

I think it's good enough to send to all early access users (that have eligible cars) and to anyone who has advanced software updates turned on. Anyone beyond that I would wait.

I find FSD V15 to be a decent bit more timid than V14, which is what we'd expect with a first big version release, which then gets polished out with the dot releases.

The release notes said school zone speed control has improved, but that doesn't seem to be the case in my area based on my testing today. I went through two school zones 5 times to test it. Navigation and some parking behaviors still need work too. I noticed a slight improvement to nag on Hurry and Mad Max modes, but not a huge change. It nags as soon as 35 seconds in some cases on side streets.

One interesting thing that happened today: I was parked in a multi-level parking garage, turned on FSD with my destination already set in navigation, and for some reason it started driving up the parking garage instead of toward the exit lol.

Tesla Reality View, pothole avoidance and pulling into home garages are definitely the stars of the show so far for V15. Those things are great. I really hope we can see specific parking spot selection soon, because that would improve the FSD experience a lot.
